![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/b0aa7d362596dcea976fead0467b9eb76c04b85c02c55dbd12e9a95652eda276.png)

The region enclosed by the curves $y=x$ and $y=\sqrt{x}$ for $y\in [0,1]$ is rotated $2\pi $ radians about the line $x=3.$ Find the volume of the resulting solid.
question.worked_solution:
First, since we are rotating about a vertical line, we need to solve the equations of our curves for $x:$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}y=x & \,⟹\,x=y \\ y=\sqrt{x} & \,⟹\,x={y}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, let's draw a horizontal arrow through the given region. The arrow should be pointing away from the axis of rotation.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/f15165acc18f4cf828671e3f9085274b26598a643be9eeb97be617272d7008d7.png)

The horizontal arrow 

- *enters* the region through the inner curve $x=y,$ and

- *leaves* through the outer curve $x={y}^{2}.$

Next, we can find the volume of our solid as the difference between the volumes of the solids generated by the outer and inner curves.

- **Step I.** Figure out the volume generated by the outer curve $x={y}^{2}.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/54820b3b386c9a435de04e0b3f07d4e2221a3e026ba5ba93ca25fa6640aa0ab1.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{outer}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[\,(3)-({y}^{2})\,]}^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}{[3-{y}^{2}]}^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step II.** Figure out the volume generated by the inner curve $x=y.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/multivariable/14222582/assets/3e1a6067500f81cabeac8dc43c4c585da608ea655667dc5e00f29a6fad0dda60.png)

The corresponding volume is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}{V}_{\text{inner}} & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(\text{right})-(\text{left})\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[\,(3)-(y)\,]^{2}\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}[3-y]^{2}\,\text{d}y.\end{aligned}
$$

- **Step III.** Find the difference.

Finally, we can write the volume of the original solid as

$$
\begin{aligned}V & ={V}_{\text{outer}}-{V}_{\text{inner}} \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({(3-{y}^{2})}^{2}-{(3-y)}^{2})\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {\int }_{0}^{1}({y}^{4}-7{y}^{2}+6y)\,\,\text{d}y \\  & =\pi {(\frac{{y}^{5}}{5}-\frac{7{y}^{3}}{3}+3{y}^{2})|}_{0}^{1} \\  & =\pi [(\frac{{1}^{5}}{5}-\frac{7\cdot {1}^{3}}{3}+3\cdot {1}^{2})-0] \\  & =\frac{13\pi }{15}.\end{aligned}
$$
